sub: Named after kuwwirat, the sun “wrapped up”, in ayah 1
theme: Two themes: the Day of Judgement, when everything collapses and each soul sees its deeds, and the truth of the Quran, brought by a trusted angel to a Prophet ﷺ who is not mad.
story: One of the earliest surahs revealed in Makkah. Its opening paints the end of the world so vividly that the Prophet ﷺ said: whoever wants to see the Day of Judgement as if with his own eyes should read At-Takwīr, Al-Infiṭār and Al-Inshiqāq.

The people of Makkah called the Prophet ﷺ mad and said his message came from a devil. The second half answers them: the Quran is brought by Jibrīl, noble and trusted, and the Prophet ﷺ saw him clearly on the horizon.
Reportedly, when “for whoever wills among you to take a right course” was revealed, Abū Jahl said the matter was up to them. The final ayah answered him: you cannot will unless Allah wills.

sections.title: Sun rolled up, buried girl questioned: every soul knows what it brought
sections.meaning: Twelve “when” scenes: the sun rolled up, stars falling, mountains moved, prized camels abandoned, beasts gathered, seas ablaze, souls paired, the buried girl questioned, records opened, the sky stripped away, Hell lit and Paradise brought near. Then every soul will know what it has brought.
points: Sun rolled up, stars fall, mountains removed
Prized camels abandoned, wild beasts gathered, seas set ablaze
Souls are paired with their like
The buried girl is asked: for what sin?
Records opened, sky stripped, Hell lit, Paradise brought near
Every soul will know what it has brought
sections.matters: It lets you see the Day as if with your own eyes. Everything people relied on, from the sun to their most valued wealth, gives way, and the only thing left that matters is what each soul brought.
sections.story: No specific incident. Before Islam, some Arabs buried newborn daughters alive out of fear of shame or poverty. Ayat 8–9 show that even this hidden crime, with no one to demand justice, will be exposed.
explained: The sun is kuwwirat: folded up like a turban, its light gone. Stars scatter and fall, and mountains are torn from their places. The ʿishār, she-camels ten months pregnant and the Arabs’ most prized wealth, are left untended. Wild beasts are gathered, and the seas are set on fire.

Souls are paired, each with those who did the same deeds. The buried girl is asked what sin she was killed for, which shames her killer. Records are spread open, the sky is stripped away, Hell is fired up and Paradise brought near. Then comes the answer: every soul will know what it has brought.
teaches: Everything you rely on in this world will pass.
You will be grouped with people whose deeds match yours.
No hidden wrong escapes Allah’s justice.
What you bring with you is all that will count.
sections.hook: Twelve lines begin with idhā, “when”, across ayat 1–13 (ayah 9 is the girl’s question). Ayah 14 finally answers them. Every ayah here ends in -at: kuwwirat … uzlifat, aḥḍarat.

sections.title: Sworn by stars, night and dawn: noble Jibrīl brought the Quran
sections.meaning: Allah swears by the stars that hide by day and sweep across the night, by the night as it comes or goes, and by the dawn as it breathes. The Quran is the word brought by a noble messenger, Jibrīl: powerful, honoured by Allah, obeyed in heaven and trustworthy.
points: By the stars that retreat, run and disappear
By the night as it closes in, the dawn as it breathes
It is the word of a noble messenger
Powerful, honoured with Allah, obeyed and trustworthy
sections.matters: After the Day, the surah turns to the message that warns of it. If the messenger who brought it is noble, powerful and trusted, the Quran reached us whole and cannot be doubted.
sections.story: No specific incident. The people of Makkah doubted the Quran, and this oath answers them by praising the angel who brought it.
explained: Al-khunnas al-jawār al-kunnas: stars that hold back and hide by day, run their courses and vanish as they set. They are either all the stars or the planets that seem to wander. The night ʿasʿas, closing in or departing, and the dawn tanaffas, breathing as light spreads.

The oath’s point: the Quran is qawlu rasūlin karīm, the word carried by Jibrīl. He is dhū quwwah, mighty in strength; makīn, of high rank with the Lord of the Throne; muṭāʿ, obeyed by the angels in heaven; and amīn, trusted to add nothing and leave nothing out.
teaches: The Quran reached us through the most trustworthy hands.
Night and dawn are signs worth pausing over.
A message is as reliable as its messenger.
Trustworthiness is among the qualities Allah praises most.
sections.hook: Ayat 15–18 swear by stars, night and dawn; the night and dawn lines rhyme: ʿasʿas, tanaffas. Then five words describe the messenger: karīm, dhī quwwah, makīn, muṭāʿ, amīn.

sections.title: Your companion ﷺ isn’t mad: he saw Jibrīl, and the Quran reminds
sections.meaning: The Prophet ﷺ is not mad. He truly saw Jibrīl on the clear horizon, he holds back nothing of the unseen, and the Quran is no devil’s word. So where are you going? It is a reminder for anyone who wants to go straight, though no one wills unless Allah wills.
points: Not mad: he saw Jibrīl on the clear horizon
He withholds nothing of the unseen; no devil’s words
A reminder for whoever wants to go straight
But you only will what Allah wills
sections.matters: It answers every accusation against the Prophet ﷺ and the Quran, then puts the choice back on the listener. Guidance is offered to all, but no one reaches it without Allah’s help.
sections.story: Makkah’s leaders called the Prophet ﷺ mad, reportedly after he fainted on seeing Jibrīl in his true form. And when ayah 28 came, Abū Jahl said: “It’s up to us,” so ayah 29 was revealed.
explained: Ṣāḥibukum, your companion ﷺ, is not majnūn. He saw Jibrīl in his true form on the clear horizon, so he knows the angel who brings revelation. He is not ḍanīn, holding back the unseen, or, in another reading, ẓanīn, suspected of changing it.

Nor is the Quran the word of a shayṭān rajīm: devils cannot produce it and are kept from hearing it. Fa-ayna tadhhabūn: where has your reason gone? It is dhikr, a reminder for all, for whoever wants to go straight. Yet even that wish depends on Allah’s will.
teaches: The Prophet ﷺ conveyed everything, to rich and poor alike.
Ask yourself where you are heading, and why.
Want guidance, and ask Allah for it, since your will depends on His.
The Quran is a reminder meant for everyone.
sections.hook: Denials start with wa mā: 22, 24 and 25. The ending repeats one root: shāʾa (28), tashāʾūn and yashāʾ (29). Ayat 27 and 29 both end with al-ʿālamīn.

groups.text: The sun is rolled up, the stars fall scattering, and the mountains are moved away.
Prized pregnant camels are abandoned, wild beasts are gathered, and the seas are set ablaze.
Souls are paired with their like, and the buried girl is asked what sin she was killed for.
Records opened, sky stripped away, Hell lit, Paradise brought near. Then each soul knows what it has brought.
Allah swears by the stars that hide and run, by the night as it falls, and by the breathing dawn.
The Quran is brought by Jibrīl: noble, powerful, honoured by Allah, obeyed in heaven, trustworthy.
The Prophet ﷺ is not mad, he saw Jibrīl clearly, he hides nothing, and no devil speaks the Quran.
Where are you going? It is a reminder for all who want to go straight, but only if Allah wills.

1.explain: Kuwwirat: the sun is folded in on itself like a wound turban, rolled up and thrown down, and its light goes out.

2.explain: Inkadarat: the stars fall and scatter from the sky.

3.explain: Suyyirat: the mountains are torn from their places and blown away like dust, leaving the earth flat.

4.explain: Al-ʿishār: she-camels ten months pregnant, the Arabs’ most prized wealth. ʿUṭṭilat: left untended, because people are too terrified to care about their dearest possessions.

5.explain: Al-wuḥūsh ḥushirat: wild animals are gathered, either for Allah to settle the wrongs between them, or all mixed together in panic.

6.explain: Sujjirat: the seas are set blazing with fire, or else filled up and merged into one.

7.explain: Zuwwijat: souls are paired. Each person is grouped with those who did the same deeds, or souls are rejoined with their bodies.

8.explain: Al-mawʾūdah: a baby girl buried alive, as some did before Islam out of fear of shame or poverty. On that Day she is questioned.

9.explain: Bi-ayyi dhanbin qutilat: for what sin was she killed? She had none. Asking the victim is a severe rebuke to the one who killed her.

10.explain: Aṣ-ṣuḥuf nushirat: the records of deeds are spread open, and each person receives his in the right hand or the left.

11.explain: Kushiṭat: the sky is stripped away and removed, like skin pulled off an animal.

12.explain: Suʿʿirat: Hellfire is stoked until it blazes as never before.

13.explain: Uzlifat: Paradise is brought close to the people who will enter it.

14.explain: ʿAlimat nafsun mā aḥḍarat: this answers all the “when” lines. Every soul will know exactly what good and evil it has brought.

15.explain: Fa lā uqsimu: “So I swear.” Al-khunnas: the stars that hold back and hide during the day.

16.explain: Al-jawār al-kunnas: the ones that run their courses and then disappear, either all the stars or the five planets that seem to move backwards.

17.explain: ʿAsʿas: the night as it approaches with its darkness, or as it departs. The word can carry both meanings.

18.explain: Tanaffas: the dawn “breathes” as its light spreads bit by bit into full day.

19.explain: Innahu: the Quran is qawlu rasūlin karīm, the word delivered by a noble messenger, Jibrīl. It is called his word because he brought it down from Allah.

20.explain: Dhī quwwah: mighty in strength. ʿInda dhī al-ʿarshi makīn: of high rank and standing with the Lord of the Throne.

21.explain: Muṭāʿin thamma: obeyed there, among the angels of heaven. Amīn: trustworthy with the revelation, adding and removing nothing.

22.explain: Ṣāḥibukum, your companion, the Prophet ﷺ, is not majnūn, mad, as his enemies claimed. He was the soundest in mind and most truthful in speech.
22.why: Reportedly the Prophet ﷺ asked to see Jibrīl in his true form. Jibrīl filled the horizon and the Prophet ﷺ fainted, and the idolaters said he was mad. These ayat answered them.

23.explain: Raʾāhu: he saw Jibrīl in his true form, bil-ufuq al-mubīn, on the clear, high horizon. This was the first sighting, in Makkah.

24.explain: Bi-ḍanīn: he does not withhold any revelation, from rich or poor. In the reading bi-ẓanīn, it means he is not suspected of adding or changing anything.

25.explain: Nor is the Quran the word of an accursed devil. Devils cannot produce it and have been kept from hearing it.

26.explain: Fa-ayna tadhhabūn: so where are you going? Where has your reason gone, turning from something so clearly true?

27.explain: In huwa illā dhikrun lil-ʿālamīn: it is nothing but a reminder for all people and jinn.

28.explain: Li-man shāʾa minkum an yastaqīm: for whoever of you wants to go straight, following the truth and holding to it.

29.explain: You can only will to go straight if Allah, Lord of the worlds, wills it. His will is always done, and no one does good except with His help.
29.why: Reportedly, when ayah 28 was revealed, Abū Jahl said: “It is up to us. If we wish, we go straight; if not, we don’t.” This ayah answered him.
